docs.title: Chef iQ Sense
docs.text: Status: Complete Protocol: BLE + Wi-Fi Manufacturer: Chefman / Chef iQ Manufacturer Status: Server-dependent

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Smart thermometer hub (CQ60) with wireless probes. Uses BLE for probe communication and Wi-Fi provisioning; Wi-Fi connects to AWS IoT cloud via MQTT. The Android app is React Native with Hermes bytecode (v96), decompiled via hermes-dec to extract full protocol logic. Five BLE UUID families support thermometer probes, system configuration, Wi-Fi provisioning, user identity, and OTA firmware updates. Temperatures are IEEE 754 single-precision floats; the app applies no unit conversion in the BLE decode path, so the wire unit is whatever the writable Temperature Unit characteristic (9C6FFFC0) is set to.

docs.title: Hardware
docs.text: Property Value Models CQ60 hub (HVIN CQ60-3B-HUB, "CHEF HUB3-V2"); probes CQ60-QPR-01/02/03 ("CHEF PROBE-V2") and newer CQ60-PRC-01/02/03/04 Chipset ESP32-WROVER-E Radio BLE + Wi-Fi FCC ID Hub: 2AC7Z-ESP32WROVERE (Espressif modular approval); probes: 2A2YP-CQ60QPROBE (earlier v1 grant 2A2YP-CQ60PROBE; ISED IC 27740-CQ60QPROBE) Components TS5A3159 analog switches, TCA9534 I2C port expander, NS4168 speaker

docs.title: Pairing, registration and reset are different operations
docs.text:
The hub's power button is not a probe-pairing button, and a probe has no off switch. Do not factory-reset a hub merely because a phone or probe is already paired.

  • Passive temperature reading: remove the probe from its dock and listen for manufacturer 0x05CD advertisements. Home Assistant uses this path with no hub, cloud account, Bluetooth bond or GATT connection. Existing vendor registration does not prevent it. It is read-only and currently models only the CQ60 probe, not the hub, oven or cooker.
  • Existing hub on another phone: disconnect other phones, sign in with the owner or accepted shared account and select the existing appliance. Reuse a valid bond; if it is stale, forget only the phone's Bluetooth entry. The vendor app can also double-tap the hub's power button and create a bond. Its online registration check distinguishes owner/shared access from another manager's appliance, so a successful bond alone does not prove offline app setup.
  • Add or replace a probe: put that probe in the charging nest and use the new-probe prompt or More → Manage Probes. Command 16 registers, 17 deregisters, and attributes 24/25 report registration/dock. On failure, reseat the probe and check contacts. Gen 2 supports three probes and Gen 3 four. Resetting the hub would erase names/favorites and force every probe to be registered again.
  • Used hub from another account: request access from the existing manager first. If ownership cannot be recovered, hold a pin in the reset hole beside the power button for 3 seconds until the hub beeps and connection lights blink, then wait for reboot. Cross-account probe transfer without the old owner is not proven; a hub reset is not a universal release from a different hub's registration.

The iQ MiniOven has a separate direct Probe Cook flow: select it on the oven, remove the probe from its Smart Hub, let the oven detect it, then tap to connect. The documentation does not require deregistration first or prove simultaneous hub/oven monitoring. The iQ Cooker accepts a Sense probe except during pressure cooking; its WiFi Reset and Factory Reset are distinct.

docs.title: Wi-Fi Provisioning Flow
docs.text:
All Family C characteristics are UTF-8 strings carrying JSON. To join a network the app writes {"connect": <network>} to 8A71FFA3 (the <network> object comes from the scan entry — fields ssid/auth/rssi — extended with the entered passphrase); to forget a network it writes {"forget": "<ssid>"}.

  1. Read Network Info (8A71FFA0) — get current status
  2. Read Scanned Network (8A71FFA1) — list available networks
  3. Write Set Wi-Fi Network (8A71FFA3) — {"connect": ...} with SSID + password
  4. Monitor Wi-Fi Mode (8A71FFA4) — track connection progress
  5. Read Network Info (8A71FFA0) — confirm connected (has IP)

docs.title: Temperature Data Encoding
docs.text: All temperatures are IEEE 754 single-precision floats (4 bytes, little-endian). The app applies no unit conversion in the decode path (parseBytesData is a plain readFloatLE), so the unit on the wire is not determinable from the app code — it is governed by the writable Temperature Unit characteristic 9C6FFFC0: 0 = Fahrenheit, 1 = Celsius. No out-of-box default is evidenced; the app writes the setting from the phone locale during setup. (The connectionless advertisement path, by contrast, is always signed int16 LE in tenths of °C — see the YAML spec's device notes.)

docs.title: Wi-Fi Provisioning Protocol Versions
docs.text:
Three versions exist, selected by device capability:

  • V1: Uses MQTT topic {deviceId}/cmd/{update}, simple request/response
  • V2: Uses ciq-v2/cmd/thermometer/{cognitoId}~{deviceId}/req/{command}, versioned envelope
  • V3: Uses ciq-v3/cmd/oven/{cognitoId}~{deviceId}/{command}, same envelope as V2

docs.title: CHEMION LED Glasses / CHEMION HAT
docs.text: Status: In Progress Protocol: BLE Manufacturer: CHEMION (CoolLED OEM hardware; companion app by Neofect) Manufacturer Status: Unsupported

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
CHEMION glasses are sunglasses with a 9×24 LED matrix across the front; the CHEMION HAT is a cap with a 12×32 colour LED matrix. Both are driven from the CHEMION phone app (Android package com.neofect.chemion), which doubles as a design tool and a storefront for downloadable content packs. The store and login live in the vendor cloud — the control protocol does not. Everything the app does to the device is one BLE frame protocol, fully mapped here from the app (v3.0.5) and cross-checked against public 2015 reverse engineering (gsuberland/ChemionHacking). That earlier work left the packet checksum unsolved; it is a plain XOR over the payload bytes.

A replacement app can scan, connect, stream frames, upload designs to device slots and read battery without any vendor service.

docs.title: Hardware
docs.text: Property Value Models CHEMION Original (glasses), CHEMION HAT (cap) Chipset Nordic nRF51 series (glasses; per public teardown) Radio BLE (Nordic UART Service on the glasses) Glasses matrix 9 rows × 24 cols, 2 bits per pixel, 54-byte frames HAT matrix 12 × 32, 4 bits per pixel color, 1536-byte frames Save slots ~6 (glasses) / ~144 (HAT) — inferred from app constants, unverified

docs.title: Initial Setup
docs.text:
No provisioning. Power the device on; it advertises immediately and accepts a connection from any central — no account, PIN or bonding step exists in the app flow.

Property Value Setup required No Method ble_direct Advertised name prefix CHEMION (glasses), HAT (cap); some units show CoolLED Passphrase protection not_applicable Confidence medium (from the app's connect flow; not yet replayed on hardware)

After connecting, enable notifications on the notify characteristic and send the heartbeat frame every 5 seconds — the app does this per connected device, and whether the link survives without it is untested.

Factory reset: none documented and none found in the app — there is no credential state to clear. Power-cycling drops the current connection, which is the remedy for the usual failure mode: the device is still connected to another phone (one BLE link at a time).

Rebinding to a new controller: just connect from the new one — nothing binds the device to an owner. If the old phone keeps grabbing the link, remove the device from its OS Bluetooth list so a cached bond stops auto-reconnecting.

docs.title: BLE Services
docs.text: UUID Name Description 6e400001-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e Nordic UART (glasses) Primary service, CHEMION Original 6e400002-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e Command Write Frames written here, one write per frame 6e400003-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e Notify Replies/notifications (layout unverified) 4b0d67ea-2faf-4b3c-8c53-f6af0f0171f5 HAT service Primary service, CHEMION HAT 4b0d67eb-2faf-4b3c-8c53-f6af0f0171f5 Command Write HAT frames (roles by convention, verify) 4b0d67ec-2faf-4b3c-8c53-f6af0f0171f5 Notify HAT replies (roles by convention, verify)

docs.title: Frame format
docs.text:
Every command is one frame, written in a single characteristic write:

[0xFA] [cmd] [lenHi] [lenLo] [payload …] [checksum] [0x55] [0xA9]
  • cmd is the command type: 0x01 request, 0x02 reply, 0x03 stream, 0x04 notify, 0x05 error, 0x06 identify.
  • lenHi/lenLo = payload length, big-endian.
  • checksum = XOR of the payload bytes only (header, cmd and length excluded).
  • Payloads embed a 2-byte big-endian message ID plus, almost always, a constant 0x01.

Worked example — power off: FA 01 00 03 00 02 01 03 55 A9 (payload 00 02 01, checksum 00^02^01 = 03).

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Message ID Type Payload Description 2 request 00 02 01 Power off 3 request 01 00 03 Battery level query (reply on notify char) 5 request 01 00 05 Heartbeat — send every 5 s 6 stream 01 00 06 <data> Realtime frame streaming (glasses path) 7 request 01 00 07 Slot/status query (semantics unverified) 9 notify 01 00 09 Sound-reactive streaming marker 10 request 01 00 0A <data> Frame data block (54 B glasses / 1536 B HAT) 11 request 01 00 0B <slot> <sizeHi> <sizeLo> Transfer start (glasses; HAT sends empty payload) 12 request 01 00 0C Transfer end (glasses) 13 request 01 00 0D 01 [data] Play stored frames (glasses) 14 request 01 00 0E <slot> Slot op — play/delete family (glasses) 16 request 01 00 10 <slot> Slot op — free/delete family 20 request 01 00 14 <slot> Slot-frame upload start (both types) 21 request 01 00 15 Slot-frame upload end (glasses)

Message ID 4 emits the same wire bytes as 16 (legacy alias). Three further IDs are loaded from values the static analysis could not resolve (likely 1, 8 and 15 or 17 — status, old heartbeat, delete/DFU family per the 2015 wiki).

Full byte-level frames, parameters and confidence notes are in the machine-readable spec: device-specs/devices/chemion-glasses.yaml.

docs.text: Signal Meaning Name prefix CHEMION CHEMION Original glasses — NUS service Name prefix HAT CHEMION HAT Name contains CoolLED OEM-branded unit of the same family Service 6e400001-… Glasses protocol endpoint Service 4b0d67ea-… HAT protocol endpoint

docs.title: Cloud (not needed for control)
docs.text: api.chemi-on.com and content.chemi-on.com serve the content store (fonts and sound packs as ZIP) and login/SNS features. No command travels through them.

docs.title: Open Questions
docs.text:
• Notify-channel reply layout (battery level, error frames) — parsing was not fully traced; verify with one HCI capture.
  • Which messages open/close a slot upload in practice (11/12 vs 20/21), and where frame counts and timing ride.
  • Pixel encodings: 2 bpp bit order on the glasses; 4 bpp nibble order/palette on the HAT.
  • Whether the 5 s heartbeat is mandatory to hold the link.
  • HAT realtime-streaming route (its msgId-6 path emits an empty payload in the app).
  • OTA: app v3.0.5 has no DFU path; the 2015 app had nRF legacy DFU, so old bootloaders may accept firmware — unexplored and not needed for control.

docs.title: CoolLEDX / CoolLED1248 LED Signs
docs.text: Status: In Progress Protocol: BLE Manufacturer: Juntong Technology (believed) Manufacturer Status: Unsupported

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The single most common cheap BLE LED sign family on AliExpress, Amazon and Temu — sold with no brand name, only a product-page screenshot of the CoolLED1248 app. They turn up as car rear-window signs, bike/backpack panels, name badges, bar signs and hat visors. Sizes vary from 12×48 up to long banner strips; colour capability varies from monochrome through a 7-color mode to full RGB.

The app is a pixel design tool: type text with a colour picker, drop in an image or animated GIF, or drive a music-reactive bar visualizer. The design is rendered on the phone and pushed to the sign as a bitmap.

There are at least seven hardware generations sharing the CoolLED* advertising name. Only the CoolLEDX generation ("basic protocol") is fully mapped; CoolLEDM and later use an "advanced protocol" that is largely unmapped, with a nearly identical frame structure but different command values.

docs.title: Hardware
docs.text: Property Value Advertised names CoolLED, CoolLEDA, CoolLEDX, CoolLEDS, CoolLEDM, CoolLEDU, CoolLEDUD / iLedBike, CoolLEDMX, CoolLEDUX Radio BLE Sizes Variable; CoolLED fixed 48×12, CoolLEDA fixed 32×16, CoolLEDX variable (96×16 typical) Color modes 0x00 monochrome, 0x01 7-color, 0x02 full RGB App CoolLED1248 (iOS / Android)

docs.title: Discovery
docs.text:
Scan for a device whose local name starts with CoolLED (or is iLedBike) to recognise the family. Match on the exact name to decide what to drive: only CoolLEDX is mapped, and the device spec deliberately restricts auto-discovery to it. A CoolLEDM/CoolLEDU/CoolLEDMX/ CoolLEDUX that matched a loose CoolLED prefix would be handed the basic-protocol command table, which is silently wrong on those generations.

The advertisement carries the panel geometry, so a client never has to ask the user for the sign's size:

Offset Length Description 0 6 MAC address 6 1 Height (pixels) 7 2 Width (pixels, uint16 BE) 9 1 Color mode (0 = mono, 1 = 7-color, 2 = full RGB) 10 1 Firmware version

Manufacturer data shorter than 11 bytes means the device is not a usable CoolLED*.

docs.title: BLE Services
docs.text: UUID Name Description 0000fff0-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb Control Service Primary service 0000fff1-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb Control Write commands, receive notifications

docs.title: Frame Format (basic protocol — CoolLEDX)
docs.text:
0x01 | escape( length_be16 || payload ) | 0x03
  • 0x01 start-of-frame, 0x03 end-of-frame
  • length_be16 is the unescaped payload length, big-endian, and is itself escaped
  • payload is [command byte][command data...]

Because 0x01 and 0x03 are frame delimiters, any byte below 0x04 inside the length or payload is escaped with a 0x02 prefix and offset by +4:

Raw Escaped 0x00 0x02 0x04 0x01 0x02 0x05 0x02 0x02 0x06 0x03 0x02 0x07

Escape 0x02 first when transforming a buffer, or you will double-escape the escape prefixes you just introduced.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Byte Notes Music bars 0x01 16 bytes on CoolLEDX (8 heights + 8 colors); 8 bytes on CoolLEDM Text 0x02 Rendered text bitmap payload Image 0x03 Still image bitmap payload Animation 0x04 Multi-frame payload Icon 0x05 Icon payload Mode 0x06 Display mode Speed 0x07 0x00–0xFF Brightness 0x08 0x00–0xFF Switch 0x09 Power/app on-off Transfer 0x0A Unconfirmed Invert display 0x0C Confirmed on CoolLEDM Clear (probable) 0x0D Observed on CoolLEDM followed by 28 28 28 28 28 28 28 00 Show icon 0x11 Unconfirmed Power down 0x12 Unconfirmed Button on 0x13 Unconfirmed Mirror (probable) 0x15 Unconfirmed Query 0x1F CoolLEDM replies 01 ff 00 01 00 Initialize 0x23 Takes a battery level byte; confirmed on CoolLEDM

Text, image and animation payloads are rendered client-side to the panel's advertised width/height and colour mode before being chunked into frames.

docs.title: Error Codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0x00 Success 0x01 Transmission failed 0x02 Device abnormality 0x03 Data error 0x04 Data length error 0x05 Data ID error 0x06 Data checksum error

docs.title: CoolLEDM and later ("advanced protocol")
docs.text: Same 0x01 / 0x03 framing and 0x02 escaping, but nearly every command value differs and the text/image payload encodings are opaque. Newer app versions (2.x) can import/export a .JT design file, which is a useful bridge for building content without speaking the wire protocol. This generation is not yet mapped and is the main open item on this target.

docs.title: Denon AVR-S720W
docs.text: Status: Spec Available — discovery observed on live hardware, control surface documented from published sources (not replayed here) Protocol: WiFi (HTTP /goform/ on port 80, ASCII control on port 23, UPnP MediaRenderer) Manufacturer: Denon (IEEE registers its OUI to D&M Holdings Inc.) Manufacturer Status: Active

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A 2016 7.2-channel Denon receiver, and a good example of a device whose local control is easier than its discovery. There is no account, no pairing, no token and no session: anything that can route to the receiver has full control of it. The hard part is recognising it — everything it announces on the network is a generic standard.

Four surfaces live on one address:

Surface Port What it is good for /goform/ HTTP API 80 Everything a remote does. No session, no auth. Undocumented. Denon/Marantz ASCII control 23 The same vocabulary, plus unsolicited state push. One client at a time. Vendor-published. UPnP MediaRenderer from SSDP LOCATION Handing the receiver a media URL to play — the one thing goform cannot do. AirPlay 1 + Spotify Connect from mDNS SRV Streaming sinks, not control. Their TXT records are the best identification signal the unit emits.

The two control routes carry the same commands: GET /goform/formiPhoneAppDirect.xml?PWON and a PWON\r written to port 23 do the same thing. So a consumer that speaks only HTTP loses nothing but the push — which is why every entity in the machine-readable spec binds over HTTP.

docs.title: Discovery
docs.text:
Nothing this receiver advertises is vendor-specific on its face:

  • mDNS: _http._tcp, _airplay._tcp, _raop._tcp, _spotify-connect._tcp
  • SSDP: upnp:rootdevice, its UDN, urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:MediaRenderer:1, and the three standard renderer services (RenderingControl, ConnectionManager, AVTransport)
  • Hostname: Denon-AVR-S720W.local — model-derived, but it changes when the owner renames the receiver

Three details do the identifying instead, and all three were observed live:

  1. The SSDP SERVER header reads KnOS/3.2 UPnP/1.0 DMP/3.5. KnOS is D&M's firmware platform; a SERVER containing KnOS/ promotes a generic MediaRenderer hit to a positive vendor identification before any HTTP request.
  2. The UDN's node field is the MAC — uuid:XXXXXXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-0005CDAABBCC. 00:05:CD is D&M's OUI, so a UDN ending in twelve hex digits that start 0005cd is a D&M device — a second vendor signal with no HTTP fetch, and the receiver's stable identity. It is not a join key against the AirPlay deviceid: a receiver has a wired and a wireless MAC, and the two records may carry different ones. Join an SSDP hit to an mDNS hit by address.
  3. The Spotify Connect cpath is /goform/spotifyConfig. /goform/ is D&M's own web-API namespace — this is the strongest single mDNS signal on the unit, despite being a third party's protocol.

The AirPlay TXT records carry the model string in two places (am and model, both AVRS720W) and the AirPlay generation in two more (srcvers and vs, both 190.9.p6 — AirPlay 1, with no pk record, so AirPlay-2-only senders will not see this receiver at all).

Two of the three signals are machine-matchable, and the spec declares them as mdns_txt_match conditions rather than leaving them as prose: cpath equal to /goform/spotifyConfig on _spotify-connect._tcp, and a deviceid starting 00:05:CD on _airplay._tcp (with am starting AVR on _raop._tcp as a weaker third). Only the SERVER header stays prose — the schema has no SSDP-reply matcher yet. All of these say "a D&M device", never "this unit": identity is the UDN or the AirPlay deviceid value.

docs.title: Initial Setup
docs.text:
Property Value Setup required Yes — Ethernet, or on the receiver's own on-screen menu Method wired — plug into the NETWORK port, no menu interaction — or device_ui (Wi-Fi, WPS, or credentials copied over USB from an iOS device) Passphrase protection not_applicable — it is typed on the receiver, never handed to it by a client Client pairing None. There is no authentication anywhere on the local surface. Confidence medium (published sources; not run here)

The step that matters for every consumer of this spec is not the network join — it is the one after it:

Setup > Network > Network Control > Always On

With it off, the receiver's entire LAN surface — HTTP, port 23, UPnP and mDNS alike — is powered down in standby, and no client can bring it back up. No Wake-on-LAN path is documented for this generation. The trade-off is real and the user's: "Always On" raises idle draw, and Denon ships it off on some model years.

Factory reset — two different operations, and they are not interchangeable:

  • Network settings only: Setup > Network > Reset. What you want when moving to a new router.
  • Full microprocessor reset: standby, then hold TUNER PRESET CH + and TUNER PRESET CH − while pressing power, releasing when the display flashes. This also discards the Audyssey calibration — an hour of somebody's afternoon with a measurement microphone.

Neither has been performed by this project, and the front-panel button pair varies across the S-series, so confirm it against the unit's own manual first. Rebinding to a new network never needs a reset: re-run Setup > Network > Connection, and note that Ethernet takes precedence over Wi-Fi automatically when a cable is present.

docs.title: Reading state
Sending commands
docs.text:
Method Path Description GET /goform/formiPhoneAppDirect.xml?<CMD> Any ASCII command, sent exactly as port 23 takes it, with no terminator. GET /goform/formiPhoneAppPower.xml?1+PowerOn Power on/standby for zone 1. GET /goform/formiPhoneAppVolume.xml?1+-40.0 Absolute volume in dB. GET /goform/formiPhoneAppMute.xml?1+MuteOn Mute on/off.

The ASCII vocabulary is PW (unit power), ZM (main zone), MV (volume), MU (mute), SI (input), MS (surround), SLP (sleep timer) and PS (audio parameters); appending ? queries instead of setting.

Control GETs answer 200 with an empty or stub body whether or not the command was meaningful. The response acknowledges receipt, not effect — re-read a status document to find out what actually happened.

docs.title: Things that bite
docs.text:
• Volume is expressed two different ways on two routes that both work. The status documents and formiPhoneAppVolume.xml use signed dB. The ASCII MV command uses an offset integer where 80 is the 0 dB reference — the two differ by 80 (dB = MV − 80), and a third digit is a half step (MV505 = −29.5 dB). So a reading of −20.0 goes back as −20.0 on the goform route but as MV60 on the ASCII one; send MV20 instead and you get −60 dB. −40 dB is the one level where both encodings share their digits (−40 dB is MV40), so testing the round-trip at −40.0 passes through the wrong route and hides the bug. Test at −20.0.
  • At minimum volume the receiver reports the literal string --, not a number. Parse defensively.
  • VolumeDisplay: Absolute changes only the front panel. MasterVolume is still relative dB; do not add 80 to it.
  • Mute is lower case when read (on/off) and upper case when written (MUON/MUOFF). Compare case-insensitively.
  • Port 23 takes exactly one client. Holding it locks out the vendor app and every other integration on the network. Treat a connection refusal as "someone else has it", not as the device being down.
  • The HTTP server serialises requests. Firing several at once produces timeouts and resets that look like the device being offline. Send sequentially, allow seconds, retry once.
  • Surround-mode selection is a request, not a setting. The receiver substitutes based on the incoming stream and reports the substitution with no error. Show SurrMode, never the value you sent.
  • The input list is per-unit. <InputFuncList> is authoritative; <RenameSource> holds the user's labels, positionally alongside it. Send the wire token, show the rename.
  • There is no HEOS here. HEOS Built-in arrived on the 2018 AVR-S750H and the X-series H models. On an AVR-S720W, TCP 1255 is closed, and a closed 1255 is the expected result rather than a fault.
  • Single zone. The Zone2/Zone3 documents and the Z2/Z3 command prefixes belong to the family, not to this model.

docs.title: Security note
docs.text: There is no authentication on any local surface. Network reachability is the access-control model: anything that can route to port 80 or port 23 can power the receiver on at 3 a.m. at whatever volume it likes. A consumer should say so rather than imply a credential protects it.

docs.title: devolo Home Control
docs.text: Status: Spec Available (from public sources; not replayed against hardware) Protocol: Z-Wave Plus EU (868.4 MHz), manufacturer ID 0x0175 Manufacturer: devolo AG (Aachen, Germany) Manufacturer Status: Shutdown — Home Control cloud switched off 2025-12-31

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
devolo Home Control was a German-market Z-Wave smart-home system (launched 2015): a Z-Wave-to-IP gateway (the MT2600 "Zentrale") plus ~14 device SKUs, all of them rebadged standard Z-Wave Plus devices. devolo announced the end in a press release dated 2025-08-21: the Home Control servers shut down on 2025-12-31, and they did.

This is the cleanest possible rescue case: every device except the hub is a standard Z-Wave slave and works with any third-party Z-Wave controller. No firmware work, no exploits — exclude, re-include, rebuild automations.

docs.title: What died, what still works
docs.text:
Function State after 2025-12-31 Vendor app + web portal Dead; app delisted from the stores Remote access, voice control, notifications Dead Reconfiguration (rules, scenes, schedules, adding devices) Dead — even local management always went through the cloud Pre-programmed schedules and if/then rules Still execute locally on the MT2600 ("autopilot"), until something needs changing mydevolo account backend Still running (no announced shutdown date, "no guarantee" per Home Assistant) Home Assistant devolo_home_control integration Alive as a stopgap: local API on the gateway (mprm REST/WebSocket), but the credentials come from mydevolo — when that dies, it dies

The official successor is ROCKETHOME: a paid migration service that moves the hub into its own subscription cloud — 99 €/year plus ~30 € one-time activation (rockethome.de/devolo-landingpage). Rules and scenes are not migrated and the supported-device whitelist has gaps. Home Assistant's shutdown alert notes the ROCKETHOME service is not compatible with the HA integration and recommends manual migration to Z-Wave JS instead.

docs.title: The app
docs.text: com.devolo.homecontrol — delisted from the store fronts at the shutdown, but the APK still downloads via the Play API by package id (checked 2026-08-04 with apkeep; sha256 starts d6115cd03e19ae69). Not worth rescuing: static inspection shows a cloud-only Retrofit REST + RxWebSocket client (de.devolo.mprm.*) against homecontrol.mydevolo.com and *.devolo.net — there is no local control surface in the app. The gateway's local API is already documented by devolo_home_control_api, the library behind the HA integration.

docs.title: SKU → OEM mapping
docs.text:
All devices report Z-Wave manufacturer ID 0x0175 (373, "devolo Home Control" — see OpenZWave's manufacturer_specific.xml). The OEM identities below come from the openHAB/OpenSmartHouse Z-Wave device database, which files several devolo devices under their OEM thing-types. Confidence is reported throughout — transcribed, not lab-verified.

devolo SKU Device OEM identity MT02600 Zentrale (gateway) devolo own design — the only e-waste item MT02646 Smart Metering Plug (1st gen) Philio PAN11 MT02792 Smart Metering Plug (2nd gen) Philio PAN11 family MT02647 Motion Sensor Philio PST02-1B (motion + temp + lux) MT02648 Door/Window Contact Philio PST02 family (contact variant) 09813 Smoke Detector unverified (Philio-style command classes) MT02755 Humidity Sensor (temp + humidity) unverified (Philio-style) MT02756 Water/Flood Sensor unverified (Philio-style) MT02652 Wall Switch (2 rockers, battery) Z-Wave.me wall-controller family (also POPP) MT02653 Key Fob (4 buttons) Z-Wave.me KFOB (manual text is the KFOB's verbatim) MT02759 Flush-Mount Switch (in-wall relay) Qubino-derived flush module MT02761 Shutter Control (in-wall) Qubino-derived (Flush Shutter family) — Flush-Mount Dimmer Qubino-derived (Flush Dimmer family) MT02650 (art. 09356) Radiator Thermostat Danfoss — filed under manufacturer Danfoss in the database; LC-13 family

docs.title: Migration cheat-sheet
docs.text:
The universal pattern: put the new controller into exclusion mode and run the device-side exclusion procedure — this works even though the old network is dead, because exclusion is initiated on the device. Then include normally. Keep battery devices awake during the interview or it stalls.

Device Exclude Include Factory reset / notes Metering Plug MT02646 Front button 3× in 2 s same — Metering Plug MT02792 ON/OFF button 3× in 1.2 s auto-inclusion ~2 min after power-up, or 3× in 1.2 s Hold ON/OFF ≥ 10 s Motion MT02647 / Contact MT02648 Tamper key 3× in 1.5 s same Tamper key 4×, hold 4th until LED off (~3 s), release within 2 s Smoke Detector 09813 Program switch ≥ 1 s same The fiddly one: battery out/in, seat in mount, then press the transparent button; success = yellow LED + beep. Expect retries (community thread) Humidity MT02755 Tamper key 3× in 1.5 s first power-on does Network Wide Inclusion — Flood MT02756 Tamper key 3× in 1.5 s same — Wall Switch MT02652 Any button 1 s same — Key Fob MT02653 Management mode: button 3, then short press 3 Fresh: hold button 1 for 1 s Management mode: button 3, then hold button 4 ~5 s. Re-do associations on the new network Flush Switch MT02759 Toggle I1 3× in 5 s (params kept) auto ~2 min after power-up, or I1 3× in 5 s I1 5× in 5 s within 60 s of power-up. Service button S only on 24 V SELV Shutter MT02761 Toggle I1 3× in 3 s same Re-run position calibration after migrating Flush Dimmer I1 3× in 3 s auto ~2 min, or I1 3× in 3 s Never use the S button on 110–230 V mains Thermostat MT02650 Short press middle button same Reported LC-13 recovery: batteries out, hold middle button while reinserting. Check your new controller can set the temperature offset (Climate Control Schedule CC) before migrating

docs.title: Target hardware
docs.text:
• Home Assistant Green + Z-Wave stick (e.g. Connect ZWA-2) with Z-Wave JS — the migration path HA itself recommends; reported ~120–180 € total.
  • Homey Pro (~399 €) — caveat: devolo-badged Philio devices report manufacturer ID 0x0175, which current Philio Homey drivers don't match, so they pair as "Unknown Z-Wave Device"; siren/flood drivers are open community requests.
  • openHAB, homee, Hubitat, Z-Wave.me — all work; the openHAB database already contains full channel/parameter definitions for every SKU above.

Automations are rebuilt from scratch on the new system — only ROCKETHOME migrates any configuration at all, and only partially.

docs.title: Hub disposal
docs.text: The MT2600 Zentrale has no local rescue path: closed gateway, cloud-issued credentials, app dead. Options are the ROCKETHOME subscription migration or e-waste. Everything else in the estate should be migrated, not discarded — the used market is flooded (hubs ~10 €, thermostats 5–22 €), which also makes these devices cheap Z-Wave spares for anyone already on Z-Wave JS.

docs.title: Drobo NAS Status Daemon
docs.text: Status: Spec Available (unverified; read-only) Protocol: LAN (TCP 5000, pushed XML) Manufacturer: Drobo (StorCentric) Manufacturer Status: Shutdown — sales ended 27 January 2023; liquidated 2023

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Drobo is gone and Drobo Dashboard is unsupported, but Drobo FS, 5N, 5N2 and B800fs units keep running their BeyondRAID arrays. The daemon behind Dashboard still pushes the whole array status to anyone who connects to TCP 5000 — no request, no login, no TLS — so a phone or monitor can show each bay's traffic-light status, warn on a failed or missing drive and track free space.

The spec is read-only on purpose. The same daemon listens on TCP 5001 and UDP 5002; one of them carries an undocumented command set that includes destructive drive operations.

docs.title: Initial Setup
docs.text: Property Value Setup required No Method Connect to TCP 5000 and read Discovery None documented (Dashboard probably used UDP 5002 broadcasts) Passphrase protection not_applicable — no authentication Confidence medium

docs.title: Protocol Summary
docs.text:
Each frame: 16-byte header, then XML.

Offset Size Field 0 8 DRINASD\0 (older firmware: DRINASD9 / DRINASDa) 8 4 Version, seen as 01 01 00 00 12 4 Body length, big-endian, counting a trailing NUL

The body is <ESATMUpdate>: mStatus (0x8000 OK, 0x8004 yellow, 0x8006 red, 0x8240 relayout…), protected capacity in bytes, thresholds, and one <nX> record per bay under <mSlotsExp> with its status (3 green, 2 yellow, 1 red, 0x80 empty, 0x86 failed), drive make, serial and size. It repeats every 10–20 s while the socket is open.

The 16-byte header layout comes from one owner's reading of a single 5N2, with no published capture; the two exporters skip the header by searching for the XML start.

See device-specs/devices/drobo-nasd-status.yaml for the full spec.

docs.text:

docs.title: Dyson Air Purifier
docs.text: Status: Local discovery and MQTT topic structure documented Protocol: WiFi (mDNS + local MQTT broker on port 1883) Manufacturer: Dyson Manufacturer Status: Active

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Dyson purifier models advertise a local MQTT broker. The device is the broker, and topics are scoped by serial number. The broker login is the device serial plus a hash of the Wi-Fi password printed on the machine's sticker; models without a sticker (roughly 2020 onward) get the same credential from the MyDyson account instead. No button press or pairing window is involved.

docs.title: Discovery
docs.text:
Browse _dyson_mqtt._tcp.local. on port 1883. The hostname contains the serial number, such as F3H-US-XXXXXXXX.local.

Use:

python scripts/dyson_discover.py --timeout 5

docs.title: MQTT Topics
docs.text:
Topic Direction Description <serial>/status/current Subscribe Current purifier state <serial>/status/connection Subscribe Connection/availability state <serial>/command Publish Power, mode, fan, oscillation, humidifier commands

Home Assistant: the core Dyson integration speaks this same local MQTT protocol once device credentials are known.

docs.title: Ecosense / FTLab RadonEye RD200
docs.text: Status: Spec Available (source-derived; untested on hardware here) Protocol: BLE GATT, two incompatible generations Manufacturer: FTLab Co., Ltd. / Ecosense Manufacturer Status: Active

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The RadonEye RD200 is a mains-powered environmental radon monitor that works directly with a phone over BLE. The vendor says it has no cloud/server service. Two public clients establish two distinct protocol generations: older units return little-endian float32 pCi/L values, while newer units return little-endian uint16 Bq/m³ values with different framing.

This document covers RD200 only, not RadonEye Pro, RadonEye Plus, EcoQube or EcoQube Flex. The newer Ecosense app for EcoQube Flex is not an RD200 protocol client. No physical device or owner reading was used for this spec.

Environmental measurements

A numeric BLE value is not by itself a medical or radiation-safety determination. Device vibration/status can affect validity, and not all status values are decoded. Preserve malformed and unavailable values as unknown, follow the actual unit's manual and current local guidance, and do not use one reading as a sole safety interlock.

docs.title: Hardware and generation identification
docs.text:
Property Value Model RD200 Radio Bluetooth LE Power External 12 V supply in the reviewed manuals; no battery telemetry is established Evidence Public clients and manuals; no capture by this project

Select a generation using both the advertised name and discovered GATT shape. Never send a command merely to discover which generation is present.

Generation Name evidence GATT evidence V1 / older FR:R2* Custom service 00001523-1212-efde-1523-785feabcd123 V2 / newer FR:RU*, FR:RE*, FR:GI*, FR:H*, FR:RD*, FR:GL*, FR:GJ*, FR:I*, FR:J*, FR:K* Write 00001524-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb; notify 00001525-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb

The V2 parent service UUID is not established. Do not invent it from V1 or treat every unknown FR: prefix as V2. A reported controller change around November 2021 is not a universal manufacturing cutoff.

docs.title: Initial Setup
docs.text:
Property Value Setup required No account, Wi-Fi provisioning or application key Method ble_direct: identify generation, subscribe, then query Passphrase protection not_applicable Confidence medium — three working clients (rd200v2, radonpy, ESPHome) connect without pairing; OS bonding behaviour unrecorded

Only one phone can connect at a time. Close the vendor app or previous client before connecting. Neither public client implements an application PIN/key exchange, but that does not prove every OS and firmware combination avoids bonding; no fixed pairing code is documented.

Factory reset: no full factory reset or dedicated hardware reset button is documented. The app data reset and V1 command 0xE0 erase stored measurements; that is not a harmless reconnect operation and does not establish a full settings/calibration reset.

Rebinding: close the previous client and reconnect directly. There is no Wi-Fi network membership to migrate.

docs.title: GATT map
docs.text:
UUID Role 00001523-1212-efde-1523-785feabcd123 Custom service 00001524-1212-efde-1523-785feabcd123 Control writes 00001525-1212-efde-1523-785feabcd123 Normal command responses / measurement notifications 00001526-1212-efde-1523-785feabcd123 Separate history stream

A simple query is one command byte. A parameterized write and a normal response use:

[command][payload_length][payload]

Subscribe to the response characteristic before writing a query. Check the response command and complete declared payload before decoding. History uses its own characteristic and does not follow the normal response path.

docs.title: Measurement response 0x50
docs.text:
A complete response has a 16-byte payload (18 bytes including its two-byte header). The payload structure is <fffHH:

Payload offset Type Meaning 0–3 float32 LE Current concentration, pCi/L 4–7 float32 LE One-day average, pCi/L 8–11 float32 LE One-month average, pCi/L 12–13 uint16 LE Pulse count 14–15 uint16 LE Previous/10-minute pulse count

Require all 16 payload bytes; one public client's shorter length guard is a bug. NaN/infinity/sentinel policy is not established, so non-finite values must not become numeric readings.

Constructed vector:

50 10 00 00 20 40 00 00 60 40 00 00 90 40 32 00 3c 00

This decodes to current 2.5 pCi/L, daily 3.5, monthly 4.5, pulse count 50 and previous count 60. It is a protocol vector, not a person's environmental data.

docs.title: Status response 0x51
docs.text: The 14-byte payload is <BBIIf: device status, vibration status, uint32 process time (interpreted as uptime minutes by the other client), uint32 raw DC value, and float32 peak pCi/L. Status enumerations and the DC conversion are unknown; do not invent them.

docs.title: Other V1 commands
docs.text:
Command Operation 0xA1 Clock write: six bytes for two-digit year, month, day, hour, minute, second; persistent calendar semantics unresolved 0xA2 Unit write: one byte, 0 pCi/L or 1 Bq/m³ 0xA4 Serial query; response includes owner-specific data and must be redacted 0xA6 Serial-type query; first three response-payload bytes are text 0xA8 Model-name query; first payload byte unknown, remaining bytes text 0xAA Alarm write: <BfB = enabled/status, float32 threshold, interval (1 = 10 minutes, 6 = one hour, 0x24 = six hours); check units/limits first 0xAC Configuration query: <BBfB = unit, alarm status, threshold, interval 0xAD OLED uint32 query; the source says it does not seem to work 0xAF Firmware query: 64 text bytes, then optional uint32 status 0xB1 Module configuration <BIIf; exact semantics unresolved 0xB4 Protection query; response command is 0xB3, with two uint32 status fields 0xBD Display calibration float32; not a generic concentration multiplier 0xC1 Product/process-mode <BBH; semantics unresolved 0xE0 Erase long-term measurements — advanced, destructive, no documented undelete 0xE8 History information query 0xE9 Start history transfer

Parameterized writes include their payload length: a1 06 <six clock bytes>, a2 01 <unit>, and aa 06 <enabled><float32 threshold><interval>. Download and preserve history before 0xE0.

docs.title: V1 history
docs.text:
1. Send 0xE8. The first three response-payload bytes are a uint16 LE entry count and a signed byte labeled checksum. The checksum algorithm is unknown; do not claim to verify it.
  2. Subscribe to the history characteristic and send 0xE9 to control.
  3. Concatenate arbitrary notification chunks until entry_count × 2 bytes have arrived. Reject truncation rather than padding.
  4. Decode each entry as uint16 LE divided by 100. Its concentration unit is not established, so do not silently label it pCi/L or Bq/m³.

The vendor says data is recorded hourly but has no internal calendar timestamp for a dated series. Preserve relative ordering and explicitly associate the host's download time and any user-recorded start time.

docs.title: V2 protocol
docs.text:
Write one query byte to 00001524-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb after enabling notifications on 00001525-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb. Wait for the response, then stop notifications before the next query. Query measurement, identity and uptime sequentially rather than concurrently.

Query Exact response length Decode 0x50 measurement 12 bytes Bytes 0–1 unknown header; five uint16 LE values at 2–3 current, 4–5 daily, 6–7 monthly, 8–9 pulse count, 10–11 previous count 0x40 peak/identity 68 bytes Model text at 16–20, firmware text at 22–29, peak uint16 LE Bq/m³ at 51–52 0x51 uptime 16 bytes Uptime uint32 LE minutes at 4–7; no seconds field is established

Concentrations in the V2 measurement are native Bq/m³, with no extra wire multiplier. Require the exact length for each response and make its fields unavailable on a wrong-length reply. Do not copy V1's command/length envelope or history/configuration commands to V2.

Constructed V2 measurement vector:

00 00 64 00 6e 00 78 00 0d 00 0e 00

It carries current 100 Bq/m³, daily 110, monthly 120, pulse count 13 and previous count 14.

docs.title: Units and validation
docs.text:
Use the manuals' exact conversion 1 pCi/L = 37 Bq/m³. Multiplying Bq/m³ by 0.027 is only a presentation approximation. Preserve native values and round only when displaying them.

scripts/test_ecosense_radoneye_rd200_spec.py independently constructs and parses both measurement generations, status, exact lengths, malformed/non-finite inputs, unit conversion, and the advanced history-erase boundary. Passing these checks does not establish hardware compatibility.

Remaining gaps include the V2 parent service and envelope, V2 history/settings, V1 status enums and history-entry units, invalid/sentinel handling, firmware update, and physical verification across hardware/firmware revisions.

See device-specs/devices/ecosense-radoneye-rd200.yaml for the complete machine-readable commands, response formats and evidence limits.

docs.title: Elgato Key Light classic HTTP family
docs.text: Status: Spec Available (not replayed by this project) Protocol: Wi-Fi — local HTTP/JSON on TCP 9123 Manufacturer: Elgato / Corsair Manufacturer Status: Active

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Classic Elgato lights can be controlled directly on the LAN without an account or cloud connection. The local API covers power, brightness, white-point temperature on CCT models, hue/saturation on Light Strips, identification, and battery telemetry on the Key Light Mini.

The Key Light Air MK.2 is different and is not covered by this guide. It uses mutual-TLS WebSocket JSON-RPC on the same port. Do not send it plain HTTP commands. The machine-readable discovery rule requires mf=Elgato and no tls TXT key, which keeps the two transports apart even after a rename.

See device-specs/devices/elgato-key-light.yaml for discovery matchers, command bodies, entity bindings, firmware-update details and remaining unknowns.

docs.title: Covered models and capabilities
docs.text:
Model / board id Local surface Key Light (53), Key Light Air (200), Key Light MK.2 (205), Key Light Neo (210), Key Light Mini (202), Ring Light (201) CCT: on/off, brightness, mired white point Light Strip (70), Light Strip Pro (206) Colour-capable: on/off, brightness, hue/saturation, and a white point limited to 153–285 mired; read-only scene state Key Light Air MK.2 (214) Excluded — mutual-TLS WebSocket, not this API

Board ids are naming hints, not the capability test. GET /elgato/lights alone cannot tell a white-only light from a strip: a Light Strip in white mode answers with temperature and no hue, exactly like a Key Light. Decide the device type once, from GET /elgato/lights/settings (a strip reports powerOnHue; white-only lights do not) and GET /elgato/accessory-info (productName "Elgato Light Strip" or "Elgato Light Strip Pro"). Then the lights reply gives a strip's mode: hue means colour, temperature without hue means white, and scene means a running scene. Probe GET /elgato/battery-info once for the Mini's battery surface; a 404 means no battery.

docs.title: Initial Setup
docs.text:
Property Value Setup required Yes, once to join Wi-Fi Method Vendor Control Center onboarding Steady-state pairing or account None Confidence Medium — public sources and community live tests, not run by this project

Power the light, follow its Control Center onboarding flow, and wait for an _elg._tcp.local. advertisement on TCP 9123. Ordinary control then works without the vendor app or cloud. This spec does not claim an independent implementation of the classic provisioning payload.

docs.title: Factory Reset and Rebinding
docs.text:
The documented route to a new network is a Wi-Fi reset, after which the light can be onboarded again. Two procedures have vendor citations:

  • Key Light Mini: power on, hold the recessed Reset button with a small tool for 10 seconds, and release when the light flashes three times. Let it restart. Vendor instructions.
  • Key Light Neo: power on, hold Reset for at least 10 seconds until the light flashes three times, then release and wait for the automatic restart. Vendor instructions.

Reset procedures for the other models are not asserted here. Do not assume the same button location or timing across the family.

docs.title: Discovery
docs.text:
Browse _elg._tcp.local. on TCP 9123. Required TXT conditions for this spec: mf=Elgato and no tls key. TXT id is not always the MAC address; fetch /elgato/accessory-info and use serialNumber as the durable identity. An empty displayName should fall back to the mDNS instance name.

The HTTP server is effectively single-threaded. Use one keep-alive connection per light and serialize requests.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
Method Path Purpose GET /elgato/accessory-info Identity, model, firmware and Wi-Fi metadata GET / PUT /elgato/lights Read state / apply a partial state update GET /elgato/lights/settings Power-on defaults; powerOnHue marks a strip GET /elgato/battery-info Key Light Mini battery and charging data POST /elgato/identify Blink the selected light PUT /elgato/firmware-update/prepare Advanced: start a signed firmware upload PUT /elgato/firmware-update/data?offset=n Advanced: write a 4096-byte image chunk POST /elgato/firmware-update/execute Advanced: validate, select and restart

The classic API is unauthenticated. Anything that can reach the light may be able to control it, rewrite configuration or upload firmware. Keep it on a trusted LAN and do not expose TCP 9123 to the internet.

docs.title: State and control examples
docs.text:
White-only light, or a Light Strip in white mode:

{"numberOfLights": 1, "lights": [{"on": 1, "brightness": 43, "temperature": 221}]}

Light Strip in colour mode:

{"numberOfLights": 1, "lights": [{"on": 1, "hue": 200.0, "saturation": 100.0, "brightness": 50}]}

A successful PUT /elgato/lights returns the full new state. Partial bodies are intentional; do not replay fields the user did not change.

Action JSON body On {"lights":[{"on":1}]} Off {"lights":[{"on":0}]} Brightness 50% {"lights":[{"brightness":50}]} White point 221 mired {"lights":[{"temperature":221}]} Hue 200°, saturation 100% {"lights":[{"hue":200,"saturation":100}]}

Use brightness 3–100, and temperature 143–344 mired on white-only lights but 153–285 mired on a Light Strip (Home Assistant's limits for the two). on is an integer 0/1, not a JSON boolean. Brightness zero does not switch the light off; it leaves on=1 with no visible output. Clamp client-side because range handling is not consistent across models.

A brightness-only write to a Light Strip in white mode makes it jump back to colour mode. Home Assistant's integration therefore resends the current temperature with every brightness write in white mode, for example {"lights":[{"brightness":50,"temperature":200}]}; do the same.

A running Light Strip scene needs special care: a bare power, brightness or colour write discards it, and there is no scene-list endpoint. The scene entity is therefore read-only in this spec. Cache the complete observed scene before implementing any scene-preserving write or restore flow.

docs.title: Firmware Update
docs.text:
Elgato runs no separate firmware service: images ship inside the Control Center application. Its public release index at https://gc-updates.elgato.com/ points at the current macOS build, and python-elgato reads the per-board images straight out of that zip. On a battery light, connect power first; python-elgato refuses to start an update on battery below 20%.

Classic models accept a complete, board-specific vendor image through the three advanced update endpoints. Images carry a 128-byte header and an Ed25519 signature. The community firmware analysis describes an inactive-slot update whose previous image remains available until successful activation. This project has not exercised an upload or power-loss recovery; do not treat that recovery claim as verified for every model or interruption point.

docs.title: EmazingLights Spectra
docs.text: Status: Research Protocol: BLE Manufacturer: EmazingLights Manufacturer Status: Abandoned (app delisted; firmware backend dead)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
EmazingLights Spectra is a programmable LED glove set for gloving light shows. The system has two halves: the gloves themselves, and a Smart Hub (called "PhotoHub" in its firmware-update metadata) that bridges them to your phone. The phone never talks to the gloves directly — it sends commands over BLE to the hub, which relays them to the gloves over a proprietary 2.4 GHz radio link.

The product is orphaned: the Android app (com.emazinglights) has been delisted from Google Play, and the server that hosted firmware updates (www.facemeltcrew.com) no longer exists (verified 2026-08-25 — the domain does not resolve). The good news: everything about controlling the gloves is local. The hub speaks an unencrypted, unauthenticated BLE protocol, fully mapped from the delisted app, so a replacement app can drive the hardware without any vendor infrastructure. The app's cloud API only provided community features (sharing glove sets) and is not needed for control.

docs.title: Hardware
docs.text: Property Value Model Spectra Smart Hub ("PhotoHub") + Spectra gloves Chipset Qualcomm CSR101x family (identified via its CSR OTA service UUIDs) Radio BLE (phone↔hub); proprietary 2.4 GHz (hub↔gloves) Power Battery-powered hub (vendor recovery advice: power off or remove batteries)

docs.title: Initial Setup
docs.text:
Property Value Setup required No Method ble_direct Setup AP / advertised name Manufacturer data contains ASCII LEHUB1 + pairing-mode byte; name is user-renamable and display-only Passphrase protection not_applicable Confidence medium (static analysis of the delisted app; no live capture yet)

Power the hub and scan. The hub announces itself in manufacturer-specific advertisement data, not its name: the company-ID-plus-payload bytes spell the ASCII string LEHUB1, and the final payload byte is a pairing-mode flag — 0x01 means the hub is in pairing mode and will accept a connection. There is no PIN, no bonding and no account. Connect and write commands directly; send the exit-pairing-mode command (opcode 0x09) when finished, mirroring the original app.

Factory reset: there is no documented reset procedure and no credential state to clear — the hub holds no network configuration and no pairing bonds. The vendor's own recovery instruction for a misbehaving hub is to turn it off or remove its batteries, then power it back on; it advertises again with the pairing flag set. Whether stored modes and a custom hub name survive a battery pull is unverified (low confidence).

Rebinding to a new phone: nothing binds the hub to a phone, so just connect from the new one. If the old phone keeps auto-reconnecting and holding the link, remove the hub from that phone's Bluetooth device list first.

docs.title: BLE Services
docs.text: UUID Name Description f4db6da0-2fcf-d296-a741-42ff6328ef42 Command service All commands + OTA stream 58511d0a-2cd1-6188-5445-9f98c91be785 Command characteristic 20-byte framed commands (write) 0788ead1-3899-45ac-0346-094599b058b8 Housekeeping service Battery / firmware version / rename e3daf87b-abe9-4a8f-9a42-1f27d2faa8fd Battery Read (encoding unverified) b66dac3c-da9d-dabe-524b-32c864bbba0e Firmware version Read; hex int, high byte = major, low = minor cba9b4f5-bfed-959d-5741-bf7340d19491 Hub name Read/write; rename writes name chars as ASCII hex 8a97f7c0-8506-11e3-baa7-0800200c9a66 OTA service Qualcomm CSR firmware-update family 210f99f0-8508-11e3-baa7-0800200c9a66 OTA new image 12-byte image header 2691aa80-8508-11e3-baa7-0800200c9a66 OTA image content 16-byte blocks 2bdc5760-8508-11e3-baa7-0800200c9a66 OTA expected sequence Block flow control

docs.title: Command frame format
docs.text:
Every command is a fixed 20-byte frame written to the command characteristic:

Offset Length Description 0 1 Header 0x55 1 1 Opcode 2 1 Index / parameter 3–18 16 Payload, zero-padded 19 1 Checksum: XOR of bytes 0–18

Writes are plain GATT writes (no encryption, no authentication). When sending a multi-frame upload, pace frames at one per 200 ms — that is the timing the original app uses.

docs.title: Commands (opcodes)
docs.text:
Opcode Name Payload Description 0x01 writeModeSettings [numColors, patternCode, 0, motionType, 1, threshold, low, medium, high] Mode header; pattern code 0xFF = custom pattern (send 0x07 next) 0x02 writeBlockSettings [blockIndex, R, G, B, 0, 1] One color of the sequence; one frame per color, in order 0x03 changeDisplayMode [mode] App sends [1] after an upload ("show uploaded mode") 0x04 changeRunMode index 1, payload [0, 0] Start running the uploaded mode 0x05 setPWMColor [R, G, B] Set a direct color immediately 0x07 flashingPatternSettings 14 bytes Custom strobe/gap/fader pattern definition 0x09 exitPairingMode all zero Leave pairing mode 0x0A syncStarted index 1 = start, 2 = end Brackets a sync/OTA session

A full mode upload is: 0x01 → one 0x02 per colour → optional 0x07 → 0x03(1) → 0x04. Opcode 0x06 is skipped in the app and presumed reserved.

docs.title: Firmware updates (OTA)
docs.text: The hub implements the documented Qualcomm CSR OTA service, and the updater flow is known: CRC32 the image (zero-padded to a 16-byte multiple), write a 12-byte header [CRC32 LE][length LE][00 10 01 08], bracket with syncStarted, stream 16-byte blocks, abort on a 10-second stall. In practice this is moot today: the vendor's firmware host is dead, so no image is available to flash unless one is recovered from the community.

docs.title: Open Questions
docs.text:
• Exact company-ID/payload split of the LEHUB1 manufacturer data (one real advertisement capture settles it).
  • The built-in flashing-pattern code table (lives in the app's bundled database; not yet extracted).
  • Battery characteristic encoding (percent vs voltage).
  • Whether the hub requires the 0x09 exit-pairing handshake before accepting mode writes, and whether the command characteristic notifies.
  • changeDisplayMode / changeRunMode operand semantics beyond the values the app always sends.

docs.text:

docs.title: Ember Mug
docs.text: Status: Complete Protocol: BLE Manufacturer: Ember Technologies Manufacturer Status: Server-dependent (telemetry to collector.embertech.com; BLE control works locally)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Temperature-controlled drinkware family including Ember Mug 2 (10/14 oz), Travel Mug 2/2+, Cup (6 oz), and Tumbler (16 oz). Reverse engineered via APK decompilation by the community. Full BLE control works without the cloud.

UUID (short) Name Properties Description 0x3622 Mug Service - Primary service (Mug/Cup/Tumbler) 0x3621 Travel Mug Service - Primary service (Travel Mug) 0x0001 Mug Name R/W UTF-8, up to 14 bytes 0x0002 Current Temperature R uint16 LE, value * 0.01 = degrees C 0x0003 Target Temperature R/W uint16 LE, value * 0.01 = degrees C; 0x0000 = heater off 0x0004 Temperature Unit R/W 0x00 = Celsius, 0x01 = Fahrenheit 0x0005 Liquid Level R 0 = empty, 30 = not empty 0x0006 Date Time Zone W 4-byte Unix timestamp LE + 1-byte TZ offset 0x0007 Battery R byte 0: percent (5-100), byte 1: on charger (0/1) 0x0008 Liquid State R 0=standby, 1=empty, 2=filling, 4=cooling, 5=heating, 6=stable 0x000C Firmware R 3x uint16 LE: firmware, hardware, bootloader version 0x0012 Push Event R/N Event ID (1-9) triggers re-read of related characteristic 0x0014 LED Color R/W 4 bytes: R, G, B, brightness (0-255 each)

docs.title: Enel X Way JuiceBox (JuiceNet UDP)
docs.text: Status: Spec Available (unverified) Protocol: WiFi (UDP, charger-initiated; telnet console on TCP 2000) Manufacturer: Enel X Way North America (formerly eMotorWerks) Manufacturer Status: Shutdown — apps and servers switched off 2024-10-11

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The JuiceBox is a 240 V Level 2 EV charger whose smart features — above all changing the charging current — ran through Enel X's JuiceNet cloud. Enel X Way announced on 2024-10-02 that it was leaving the US and Canada and turned the apps and servers off nine days later. Every unit still charges at the current it was last set to; nothing can change that unless something on the LAN takes the server's place.

It can, because the charger never needed the cloud to be clever. It opens a UDP "stream" to a configured host and port and sends a short ASCII status line every 9–30 seconds. The server answers each line with a CMD line carrying two current limits, the time of day and a counter, protected by a three-character base-35 hash. A LAN host that receives those datagrams can read current, voltage, energy and plug status, and by replying can set the online limit (0 pauses charging) and the offline limit the unit falls back to.

Two things this spec cannot do: decode the encrypted variants (v09e on generation 2 from June 2024, v08 on generation 1 from mid-November 2024, with a move to port 9004) — a unit kept off the internet stays plaintext — and protect your wiring. The charger clamps to its own rating, not to the circuit behind it; the spec carries a safety_advisory and marks both current commands advanced.

docs.title: Hardware
docs.text:
Property Generation 1 (2016–2019) Generation 2 "Next Gen" (2020–) Models JuiceBox Pro 32 / 40 / 40 Lite / 75 JuiceBox 32 / 40 / 48 Chassis Metal, four screws Plastic Wi-Fi module ZentriOS WZ (PCB 8.12–8.17) Gecko OS on Silicon Labs WGM160P (PCB 9.x) Firmware string EMWERK-JB_1_1-… / EMWERK-JB814-… EMWERK-JB201-1.0.46 / -1.0.69 Protocol v07 (encrypted: v08) v09u (encrypted: v09e) Telnet (TCP 2000) Yes 1.0.46 yes; 1.0.69 disabled

Pre-2016 "legacy" units do not run the Zentri stack and are out of scope.

docs.title: Initial Setup
docs.text:
Property Value Setup required Yes — on Wi-Fi, and the UDP stream pointed at a LAN host Wi-Fi join softap_http: setup AP JuiceBox-### / JuiceNet-### / EXW-###, passphrase GoElectric, web form at the module's address (also setup.com) for 2 minutes after power-up Re-point routes (pick one) DNS override of the server name (primary); router destination-NAT + masquerade; telnet stream_close / udpc on TCP 2000 (reverts within minutes unless re-applied) Discovery None — the charger initiates; its address is the datagram source, its identity the 28-digit ID the line begins with Passphrase protection plaintext HTTP on a WPA AP with a published passphrase Confidence medium (juicepassproxy's daily practice; not replayed here)

Block directory-api.emotorwerks.com whichever route you take: its reply is what switches a unit into the undecodable encrypted mode.

Factory reset: none documented in either manual (applicable: unknown). The setup AP re-appears for two minutes after every power-up, so new Wi-Fi credentials never need one.

Rebinding to a new network: power-cycle, join the setup AP within two minutes, submit the new network. The old network need not exist. The UDP target is kept; recreate the DNS override or router rule on the new network.

docs.title: Protocol Summary
docs.text:
Status line (charger → host), every 9 s charging / 30 s idle:

<28-digit id>:v09u,s001,F31,u00412974,V2400,L00004262804,S02,T28,M0024,C0040,m0040,t09,i23,e-0001,f5990,r99,b000,B0000000,P0,E0004501,A00161,p0996!ZYK:

Fields are <letter><integer> tokens; parse by letter, never by position.

Field Meaning Scale / unit V line voltage ×0.1 V A charging current (absent when unplugged) ×0.1 A f line frequency ×0.01 Hz p power factor ×0.001 T internal temperature °C L / E lifetime / session energy Wh S 0 unplugged · 1 plugged in · 2 charging · 5 error — M / C / m online limit in force / offline limit (v09 only) / unit rating A i / e 15-minute slot 0–95 / energy in it Wh t report interval s F, r, b, B, P, X, Y unknown —

Reply (host → charger), one per status line:

CMD<d><HHMM>A<online>M<offline>C006S<counter>!<crc>$
e.g.  CMD31830A0016M040C006S001!RAS$

d weekday (0 = Sunday), HHMM local time, A online amps (4 digits on v09, 2 on v07; 0 pauses), M offline amps (EEPROM; 3 / 2 digits), C006, S counter 001–999. No reply for ~5 min → the unit falls back to M.

Hash: h = (h ^ ((h<<5) + (h>>2) + ord(c))) & 0xFFFF over the payload before !; h mod 35³ as three base-35 digits, least-significant first, alphabet 0-9 A-N Z P-Y (digit 24 is Z; O never appears). scripts/test_enel_x_juicebox_spec.py holds the spec's frames and six server-captured CMD frames from juicepassproxy to that rule.

Console (TCP 2000, prompt >): list shows # 1 UDPC host:port (n); stream_close 1 then udpc <host> <port> re-points the stream; set udp.client.remote_host / remote_port + save + reboot persist it (with a reported risk of not getting the old target back); network_lookup <name> confirms a DNS override.

See device-specs/devices/enel-x-juicebox.yaml for the full machine-readable spec.

docs.title: Enphase Envoy
docs.text: Status: Local discovery and production endpoints documented Protocol: WiFi (mDNS + HTTP REST on port 80) Manufacturer: Enphase Energy Manufacturer Status: Active

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Enphase Envoy gateways provide local solar production telemetry over HTTP. Newer firmware may require token authentication for some endpoints, but mDNS still provides a stable serial number for discovery and identity.

docs.title: Discovery
docs.text:
Browse _enphase-envoy._tcp.local. on port 80. TXT serialnum is the stable identity; TXT protovers reports the protocol/firmware version.

Use:

python scripts/enphase_discover.py --timeout 5

The discovery script resolves the mDNS service and probes /production.json to confirm the local REST endpoint.

docs.title: Local API
docs.text:
Method Path Description GET /production.json Live production/consumption summary GET /api/v1/production Production summary (flat object: wattsNow, wattHoursToday, wattHoursSevenDays, wattHoursLifetime) GET /api/v1/production/inverters Per-inverter telemetry GET /info Gateway information

The spec's sensor entities (Solar Production, Lifetime Energy, Today's Energy) bind GET /api/v1/production as their state_command with flat dotted-path state mappings (wattsNow, wattHoursLifetime, wattHoursToday), so a generic HTTP client can poll them directly. /production.json is richer but returns a per-type ARRAY (production[i].wNow / whLifetime), which a flat path cannot name — consumers that can select array entries should prefer it, and metered units report lifetime energy only there.

Machine-readable spec: device-specs/devices/enphase-envoy.yaml

Home Assistant: the core Enphase Envoy integration consumes this local API (owner-token auth on newer firmware).

docs.title: Enphase IQ Battery (Encharge) / IQ System Controller (Enpower) — BLE
docs.text: Status: Discovery + encrypted status reads supported; other installer flows remain research Protocol: BLE (Digi XBee 3 BLE + Enphase relay payloads) Manufacturer: Enphase Energy Manufacturer Status: Active

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Enphase Ensemble storage units — the IQ Battery (formerly Encharge) and the IQ System Controller (formerly Enpower) — advertise BLE beacons named Enpower/<serial> and Encharg/<serial>. The BLE interface is provided by the units' Digi XBee 3 radio (the same radio that runs the 2.4 GHz 802.15.4 site mesh; its Silicon Labs EFR32 base explains the Silabs OUI on the MAC). Installers use this link to commission the units onto the site; it also carries live statistics and control. The gateway these units report to is documented separately in Enphase Envoy.

The mobile client supports discovery, the SRP-6a/AES unlock and read-only status queries 4, 5 and 8. Provisioning, relay/grid control and other installer writes are not exposed. No live hardware unlock has been performed, so this is implementation support rather than a connection guarantee. The recovered interface is XBee 3, not XBee Series 2 / "XBee2". Communications Kit 2 has a separate, unverified GATT and credential profile and is not covered.

docs.title: Hardware
docs.text: Property Value Models IQ Battery 3T/10T/5P (Encharge), IQ System Controller (Enpower), IQ Extender Radio Digi XBee 3 (Silicon Labs EFR32), BLE + 802.15.4 BLE identity Name Enpower/<serial> / Encharg/<serial>; MAC OUI 04:0D:84 observed live

docs.title: Initial Setup
docs.text:
Property Value Setup required Yes — installer commissioning Method ble_provisioning (BLE provisioning push) Advertised name Enpower/<serial>, Encharg/<serial> Passphrase protection SRP-6a unlock + AES-encrypted channel; generic XBee default password, manager-specific 030609 Confidence medium (app-derived; only advertisement verified on hardware)

Commissioning over BLE: connect to the XBee 3 BLE service and perform the SRP-6a unlock (XBee API frame 0x2C, user apiservice). The generic library default is password, but both provisioning-manager constructor paths for the PAN/link-key checks use 030609. Use the value for the flow being implemented rather than assuming one universal password. Then send User Data Relay frames to the radio's serial interface carrying the provisioning frames: link key push (frame type 1, [0x01][0x10][16 key bytes]), gateway serial write (type 7), and pairing/commissioning status polls (types 4/5). The 16-byte 802.15.4 link key is generated locally by the commissioning app; no cloud is needed on the BLE link itself.

Factory reset: not documented. Frame type 2 (RESET_DEV) exists but its effect is unverified — do not poke it on a live site. De-commissioning is normally done via the gateway by an installer.

Rebinding: re-running the BLE provisioning push (PAN ID, link key, gateway serial) re-joins a unit to the site mesh in place; no reset needed.

docs.title: BLE Services
docs.text:
UUID Name Description 53da53b9-0447-425a-b9ea-9837505eb59a Digi XBee 3 BLE Stock XBee 3 BLE service (public Digi protocol) 7dddca00-3e05-4651-9254-44074792c590 TX Client writes XBee API frames f9279ee9-2cd0-410c-81cc-adf11e4e5aea RX Device notifies XBee API frames (CCCD 0x2902)

XBee API frame types in play (public digi-xbee-java): 0x2C BLE Unlock, 0xAC BLE Unlock Response, 0x2D User Data Relay (client→device), 0xAD User Data Relay Output (device→client). After the SRP-6a unlock, both directions are AES-encrypted with session keys from the handshake. Enphase payloads ride in the relay frames' user-data field, addressed to the radio's serial interface (micropython interface on the IQ Extender).

docs.title: Enphase provisioning frames (inside User Data Relay)
docs.text:
Byte 0 = frame type, byte 1 = 0x00 placeholder; responses echo the type and carry the payload from byte 2 on.

Type Name Purpose 1 LINK_KEY Push 16-byte site link key ([01][10][key]) 2 RESET_DEV Device reset (effect unverified) 3 RELAY_STATES Read relay states (Enpower) 4 ZB_PAIRING_STATUS 802.15.4 pairing status 5 ZB_COMMISSIONING_STATUS Commissioning status 6 ZB_READ_LINK_KEY Read back stored link key 7 Gateway serial write Write gateway serial 8 ZB_READ_ENVOY_SN Read gateway serial (PAN ID derivation/verify) 9 READ_ENPOWER_TELEM Read Enpower telemetry

The gateway-serial write is [07][one-byte serial length][serial ASCII], so its total length is the gateway serial length plus two. The read requests are 06 00 (link key), 08 00 (Envoy serial) and 09 00 (Enpower telemetry). Responses drop those first two bytes before parsing.

docs.title: Object-model protobuf layer
docs.text:
A richer proto2 protocol (Wire classes in the app) shares the same relay channel. Envelope EnsObjMdlMessage: protover (field 1, required, VERSION_1_0), timestamp (field 2, required uint64), then a oneof payload at tags 3–63: inventory (42/43), poll (13/14 — live statistics; request is {serial_num, dm_group_id}), subscribe/publish (7–10), relay control (17/18), secondary control (15/16), grid status (27/28), Encharge SoC/phase config (32/33), sleep mode (38/39), BMU stats (40/41), manual override (60/61), events, memfault diagnostics, and more — the full tag table is in the spec. DeviceType enum: ALL_DEVICES=0, ENCHARGE_DEVICE=13, ENCHARGE_MICRO=14, ENCHARGE_CTRL=15, ENCHARGE_BMU=16, ENPOWER_DEVICE=17, ENPOWER_CTRL=18, ENBRIDGE_DEVICE=19.

Live statistics decode to per-unit records: aggregated power, state of charge, active/ready microinverter counts, LED status, BMU state, available charge/discharge power, and phase-line assignment, with nested per-BMU and per-PCU statistics.

docs.text:

  • Passive BT scan of the owner's site (2026-08-18)
  • Digi XBee 3 BLE documentation + digi-xbee-java (public prior art)

docs.title: ESPHome Node (generic)
docs.text: Status: Complete (written from ESPHome's own docs and source; untested here) Protocol: WiFi — ESPHome web server REST/SSE (:80) and native API (:6053) Manufacturer: Various — ESPHome open-source firmware Manufacturer Status: Active — local by construction, no cloud, no broker

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
ESPHome is open-source firmware that turns an ESP32/ESP8266/RP2040/nRF52 board into a locally-controlled device. It is a platform, not a product: a node can be a thermometer, a plug, a bluetooth proxy, a presence sensor, a sprinkler valve, a garage-door controller, or something its owner built on a breadboard last weekend. Every one of them advertises the same mDNS service type and speaks the same two APIs.

That is why this spec exists. _esphomelib._tcp identifies the firmware, so a consumer that maps a service type to a device spec labels every ESPHome node with whichever product spec claimed the service type first — which is exactly what happened here while ratgdo was the only claimant, and every ESPHome node on the LAN turned up as a garage-door opener.

The fix has two halves:

  • Product specs on this platform carry a mdns_txt_match on the project_name TXT record. ratgdo. is a ratgdo; nothing else is.
  • This spec is the deliberate catch-all, marked platform_fallback: true on the _esphomelib._tcp method. A node matching no product spec renders as itself — its own name, its own entities.

The catch-all flag is set on that method only. The _http._tcp method below is narrowed by a TXT condition and nothing else: _http._tcp belongs to every web server on the link, and being its fallback would rebuild this bug with printers and routers in it.

docs.title: Why integration: identify_only
docs.text: Control here is entirely possible — that is what local_access: native says — but integration records what a consumer of this registry does today, and for an unrecognised node that is: name it, show it, link to its web UI. Two things hold that line. The spec declares no entities and cannot, so a consumer has controls only once it implements runtime enumeration; and the HTTP surface is optional (web_server: is a build choice — plenty of nodes run api: alone and answer nothing on :80), so the REST grammar below is for a client that has already found one, not a promise every node has it. When a consumer implements enumeration over either API, this becomes supported with no other change to the spec.

docs.title: Telling one node from another
docs.text:
ESPHome publishes a rich TXT set on _esphomelib._tcp:

TXT key Says mac Board MAC — the stable identity key. Survives rename, reflash, DHCP move friendly_name Human name (absent when the config sets none) project_name / project_version Present only when the firmware sets esphome: project: — this is what names a product (ratgdo.v25iboard_secplus2) version ESPHome version the firmware was built with board, platform Hardware (d1_mini, ESP32) — says nothing about function network wifi / ethernet / thread config_hash Changes on every config change — never an identity key api_encryption Native API requires Noise with a PSK api_encryption_supported Build can do Noise, no key set yet, plaintext still accepted api_provisioning=zero-psk A key may be provisioned over a zero-PSK Noise connection

A node built without the native API publishes _http._tcp instead, carrying version/mac/config_hash. Two build shapes land there: one with web_server: (port 80 answers) and one with neither api: nor web_server:, which ESPHome still advertises so .local resolution works at all — and on that one nothing is listening on 80. A match on that service means "an ESPHome node is at this address", not "there is an HTTP surface here".

docs.title: The two local APIs
docs.text:
Web server (HTTP :80) — present only when the build includes web_server:, so a node that answers nothing there is normal, not broken.

Action Request Enumerate + subscribe GET /events (SSE — every entity's state on connect, then updates) Entity state GET /<domain>/<entity> (add ?detail=all for name/device/select options) Entity action POST /<domain>/<entity>/<action>[?params] Sub-device entity GET /<domain>/<device>/<entity>, POST /<domain>/<device>/<entity>/<action>

Native API (TCP :6053, protobuf) — what Home Assistant uses. Frames are length-delimited protobuf behind an indicator byte: 0x00 plaintext, 0x01 Noise (Noise_NNpsk0_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256, prologue NoiseAPIInit, 32-byte base64 PSK). Hello → Connect → DeviceInfo → ListEntities → SubscribeStates. The legacy api: password: was removed in ESPHome 2026.1.0.

docs.title: Enumeration is the whole trick
docs.text: There is no "list entities" URL. Connect to /events: the node sends one state event per entity on connect, then keeps the connection open for updates. The domain gives you the control type and the entity's name is the label — the entity list is the device. Never infer a device type from the product name, the board, or the icon.

docs.title: Addressing changed — handle both
docs.text:
Firmware URL segment State id ESPHome ≤ 2025.12 slugified object_id (/sensor/outside_temp) sensor-outside_temp 2026.1.0 – 2026.6 name first, object_id still accepted (deprecated) legacy id (+ name_id from 2026.1.3) 2026.7 name only (/sensor/Outside%20Temp) still legacy id + name_id ≥ 2026.8 name only sensor/Outside Temp, no name_id

The two boundaries are one release apart, which is the trap: on 2026.7 the URL is already name-only while id still carries the legacy form, so a client that derives its URL from id breaks on exactly that release. Read name_id first.

The robust client does not derive the identifier: read name_id if present, else id, from the /events payload and send back the form the node handed you. An identifier containing / is the new form. A wrong identifier answers 404 — never a silent no-op — so trying and falling back is also safe.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The web server has no auth by default, and where the web-OTA platform is enabled anyone who can reach the node can flash it. Upstream says so too.
  • Cross-origin browser requests to entity endpoints are rejected unless the origin matches or is allow-listed.
  • A generic client cannot know what a control does. switch/Pump, cover/Gate and light/Desk render identically. Treat cover, lock, valve, alarm_control_panel and climate actions as advanced: confirm first, show reported state, and keep them out of bulk actions.
  • Cover position is 0.0–1.0, not a percentage. Sending 50 for "half open" drives the cover fully open.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Electric unicycles from King Song, Gotway/Begode and Veteran/Leaperkim, decoded by the open-source WheelLog app. Each is a notify-stream of framed packets; brand is detected from the first packets. Fully local BLE. (The BLE serial characteristic UUID is module-specific and not asserted here.)

docs.title: Protocol Summary
docs.text:
King Song: 20-byte frame, header AA 55, type at byte 16 (0xA9 live data). Gotway/Begode: 24-byte frame, header 55 AA, footer 5A5A5A5A, type at byte 18. Veteran: header DC 5A 5C + length, CRC32 on longer frames.

See device-specs/devices/euc-wheellog-ble.yaml for the full machine-readable spec.
