docs.title: Added this week
docs.text:
Two finds from earlier sweeps and one more Do these next pick. Every spec is testing: untested; wire facts from client code are reported.

Spec Source Notes Keto-Mojo GK+ Glucose & Ketone Meter 2026-10-18 candidate Read-only BLE on a vendor-base service (0003cdd0-…-00805f9b0131): fixed request frames for unit, serial and the full record dump, and the 9-byte result record (date and time, a value in two base-100 bytes, meal marker, type: glucose, ketone or control solution) with units and scales in fields. The frame check is a hypothesis: the client only sends fixed frames, and CRC-16/MODBUS sent as nibble bytes is the one rule found that reproduces all four. No entities: one notify channel carries every reply, and a "latest reading" needs filtering the schema cannot state. Medical safety_advisory. scripts/test_keto_mojo_gk_plus_spec.py. Orbit B-hyve Bluetooth Hose Timers survey table row; 2026-10-18 status change The 20-byte handshake, the AES-128-ECB counter keystream with its sum trailer, and two families: HT25-0000 (binary mesh frames, magic 0x10) and the protobuf family (HT25G2, HT25A, HT31, HT32A, HT34A; magic 0x11, CRC-16/XMODEM over header, length and payload, which corrects upstream's prose). Zone start with bounded durations, stop, status and battery. The per-mesh network key is exported once from the owner's Orbit account and is a stored credential; every vector uses an invented key. scripts/test_orbit_bhyve_ble_spec.py. One reference project, knobunc/ha-orbit-bhyve-ble, returned HTTP 451 (unavailable for legal reasons) on 2026-10-25; nothing here depends on it. LIVISI SmartHome (SHC 1 / SHC 2) #8 Local SmartHome API: token login on 8080 with the published client constant, device, capability and state reads, POST /action for switches, dimmers, shutters and thermostats, and the WebSocket event stream (9090 on SHC 2, 8080 on SHC 1). Firmware minimums and default passwords per generation. Restart is advanced. Per-device entities are left out: the device lists are JSON arrays, which instances cannot enumerate. Status: servers off 2024-03-01 (heise, digitalzimmer); Local SmartHome since 2022-09-26; no insolvency notice found. scripts/test_livisi_smarthome_spec.py.

Schema gaps that came up, each in its spec's remaining_unknowns: a frame check sent as nibble bytes (Keto-Mojo), an encrypted envelope and a CRC-16/XMODEM role (B-hyve), and instances over a JSON array (LIVISI, as with last week's BiSecur).

docs.text: None this week. The nearest is SPAN, below, where the change is a vendor-managed API migration and nothing is being orphaned.

docs.title: New candidates — new or popular, with a local path
docs.text:
Device Status Risk Local path Public work Catch Yogasleep / Marpac Dohm Connect white-noise machine Active, but the "Marpac Connect" app looks neglected. Store reviewers call it "essentially decommissioned", which is unverified and undated. The HACS integration's latest release, v0.4.4, was committed 2026-10-17 (commits). C (drifting to B) Phone-direct BLE that needs bonding. Service 00005600-d102-11e1-9b23-00025b005aa5 has one write+notify characteristic, …5601…. Commands are ASCII ending in $ (LETTER[,ID[,VALUE]]$, lowercase to query, uppercase to set). i$ returns the device ID that every other command needs. It covers power (m/M), speed 1–10 (s/S), name, clock (T) and three schedule slots (p/P). Replies are OK$, a typed report, or Failed NN$ (protocol.md). dohm-ble (MIT; 2 stars) Small and clean, and a good one-session spec. Replies carry no request IDs, so read state back after writes. t and I come from the APK and are unproven. The app allows only one connection. The checks were against Marpac Connect for Android (v1.0.7 line) and one capture dated 2026-06-02. INIM SmartLiving alarm panels with SmartLAN/G board A new custom integration was posted 2026-10-25 (HA community). The vendor is active. C Plain HTTP to the SmartLAN/G board's own web interface on the LAN. It logs in with username, password and a user code; with the installer code the panel returns no outputs. The login token appears to be static. Covers partition arm and disarm (away, home, night), outputs, zone exclusion and alarm-memory reset. The SmartLAN/SI has no web server and is not supported. ha-inim-smartlan-g (MIT; 0 stars; endpoints in docs/protocol.md, not yet read) Tested on one SmartLiving 515, and the author asks testers to try writes only while disarmed. It is a security system, so arm, disarm and bypass must be advanced, with a security_advisory about plain HTTP and the static token. The board is slow and fragile, so requests have to be serialised. Fraimic e-ink frames (13.3" and 31.5" Spectra 6) Vendor active. On 2026-10-21 the integration opened an issue for a local stand-in for Fraimic's cloud polling and voice-upload protocol (issue #84). C Unauthenticated local HTTP image upload (/api/image on firmware ≥0.2.28, multipart /upload on older firmware, /wifi-stats). Stock firmware still needs internet reachability (a periodic TCP probe to a public DNS resolver, DNS and NTP). Blocking it can make the frame fall back to an open setup AP. ha-fraimic-eink (MIT; 1 star, 526 commits) The cloud emulator targets /api/v1/ over HTTPS for the vendor host and is only planned. The local upload path can be specced today. Note the open-setup-AP fallback in security_advisory. Low priority. SPAN smart panels (MAIN 32 now; MAIN 16/40, MLO 24/48 promised for H2 2026) SPAN's own blog says the old undocumented local APIs and dashboards "will be deprecated as of December 31, 2026" (SPAN, 2026-02-23). A community issue opened 2026-10-19 quotes the panel's own /api/openapi.json on firmware r202639: "v1 REST endpoints are deprecated and will be removed on 2026-12-31". It also says the 2026-10-14 update broke app control (a2w-control #199). B for v1 REST clients; C overall Vendor-documented replacement: eBus / Homie 5 over MQTT-TLS on TCP 8883, credentials from the REST v2 API (HOP passphrase, or the door-switch bypass), mDNS _ebus._tcp (SPAN-API-Client-Docs). span-hass (MIT); SpanPanel/span (the widely used HACS integration on the old API) Vendor-documented: link, don't spec, as with TRMNL and my-PV. Worth one line in the survey, because every v1 REST client (including the popular HACS integration) breaks at year end. Relay writes switch real breakers.

Considered and left out:

  • Plejd (ha-plejd, MIT, 0 stars): the mesh key comes from the vendor cloud, and nothing dates the work to this week.
  • MicroAir EasyStart Flex (microair-bt, MIT, hardware test 2026-09-21): an RV soft starter; not news this week.
  • BlueShark: a reverse-engineering toolkit, not a device.
  • Imou vacuum: uses the vendor Open Platform, which is cloud.
  • Anker eufy Home Security: a pure-Python integration whose local status is not stated.
  • WityPower wallbox: an existing tuya-local config.
  • Tilia's legacy heating write-up (2026-10-13): the brand is unnamed and no code is published.

docs.title: Status changes to items already listed
docs.text:
• Eargo / Lexie (targets/lexie-eargo-hearing-aids.md): both removal dates have passed, but on 2026-10-25 every listing still resolved on the US storefronts. Eargo Play com.eargo.app.android (last updated 2026-09-18) and App Store id1529890348 both still show "will be removed from the store on October 22, 2026". Lexie Play com.hearxgroup.lexie (2026-09-01) and App Store id1525380701 both still show "October 8, 2026". LINK by Eargo, Play com.eargo.link.release, is in the same state. Whether the cloud went off on 2026-10-22 is unverified: no user report or independent coverage was found. The BBB notice (BBB) remains the only primary source, and a retailer adds that the online manual archive goes offline 2026-10-30 (unverified). HearingTracker's news desk now just says "Eargo has shut down". The capture window may still be open: installs from the stores still seem possible. If any owner can help, do it now.
  • Neato Botvac (research-notes/neato-botvac-d-series.md): a self-hosted replacement cloud, Vacuula, shipped its first release in mid-October (vacuula/vacuula, AGPL-3.0, 176 stars; Adafruit, 2026-10-19 (403 to fetch); OSFY, 2026-10-21). Its README lists Gen3 D3–D7 and Gen4 D800/D8/D9/D10 as supported, which contradicts the note's line "Do not buy D8+ for local control". The original Botvac Connected is not yet supported. The README lists server ports 80 (web, API, installer), 335 (Gen3 robots) and 3443 (Gen4 robots), and a separate installer re-points each robot. An OpenNeato PR (Leicas/OpenNeato #35) hands a UART-bridged robot over to a Vacuula server. The AGPL code is for deriving facts only. The note and the survey row should be updated, and the robot-to-server protocol on 335 and 3443 could become a spec.
  • VanMoof S3/X3 (survey #4): the legacy key-export host my.vanmoof.com no longer resolves. The same v8 endpoints (/authenticate, /getCustomerData?includeBikeDetails) still answer, with the same API key, on api.vanmoof-api.com (ha-vanmoof PR #2, posted 2026-10-14, merged 2026-10-16, released as 0.16.3). This is community-reported and was tested on one account. Older key exporters pointing at the old host are now broken. The one-time key export still works.
  • Withings: no reversal. Withings defends the paywall as "a matter of survival" ("Aujourd'hui, la valeur, c'est la donnée", digital product manager Vincent Brand, via Journal du Geek, 2026-10-20). Strava sync is also covered. The European price is €9.99/month or €99.99/year, and CSV/PDF export stays free. A 200+ comment thread is on Withings' own community. The didac.dev Body+ code is still unpublished (checked 2026-10-25).
  • Samsung SmartThings API: still no source confirms that the Personal Plan or billing went live in October. The HA docs still describe it as upcoming, and no October post from Samsung was found.
  • Tesla Powerwall: pypowerwall's API.md now lists a V2026_06 query set (a Tesla-signed GraphQL/bearer path). It also cites issue #354: two UK Powerwall 3 units on firmware 26.x answered on their home LAN address with no vendor-subnet route. This is a single report and unverified; it softens the 25.10.0 "AP-only" picture (pypowerwall).
  • Senec: Verbraucherzentrale Niedersachsen (as of 2026-10-06) confirms new-customer business has stopped and open orders ship by 2026-12-31. Nothing on the app, mein-senec or the cloud.
  • No news found on TiVo SkipMode (still ends 2026-11-02, price unpublished), Sony mocopi link (2026-10-28) or Casio GSW SYSTEM (2026-10-31). The same goes for Samsung SmartThings Tracker Korea (2026-10-31), Sleep Number / SleepIQ, Enphase firmware and the Fossil Hybrid key server. docs.title: 2026-11-01 (weekly sweep)
docs.text: The routine sweep for this date. A separate research pass on the same day is logged in 2026-11-01 above.

docs.title: Added this week
docs.text:
Two Do these next picks and one category-table row that this week's news made urgent. Every spec is testing: untested; wire facts from client code or vendor notes are reported.

Spec Source Notes SolarEdge Inverters (Modbus TCP / SunSpec) category table (re-scoped from SetApp /web/v1 to Modbus, as the 2026-10-11 entry asked); news below Turning Modbus TCP on (SetApp: port 1502; display inverters: 502), unit id 1, the reported _solaredge-modbus._tcp announcement, the Modbus TCP header, the SunSpec common block at 40000 and inverter models 101/102/103 with scale factors, Synergy model 160 and meter models 201–204. Power-limit, export-limit and commit writes are advanced, with a safety_advisory. One client at a time and a 2-minute idle drop, per SolarEdge's own note. Five read-only sensors. scripts/test_solaredge_modbus_tcp_spec.py. Apple AirPort Extreme / Time Capsule / Express (ACP) #11 Bonjour _airport._tcp, the 128-byte ACP header with both Adler-32 checksums, the legacy XOR password key, SRP-6a login with AES-128-CTR session keys, the property element framing and a property catalogue. Reads (name, status, WAN address, log); rename and reboot are advanced. A security_advisory (reported) for the legacy password encoding, citing airpyrt-tools. Flashing is left out. scripts/test_apple_airport_acp_spec.py; the rules were cross-checked against node-acp's own vectors, none of which are copied in. Philips Wi-Fi Air Purifiers and Humidifiers (encrypted CoAP) #12 CoAP on UDP 5683: /sys/dev/sync counter exchange, observed /sys/dev/status, /sys/dev/control. The envelope is AES-128-CBC with key and IV taken from the MD5 of a published constant plus the counter, and an unkeyed SHA-256 trailer (the survey row's "HMAC" wording is wrong). Three key sets as variants (classic names, D03-xx, compact D03xxx), with fan, mode, speed, child lock, display, timer, air quality, humidity, water and filter entities per set. Older HTTP and plain-CoAP generations are named, not specified. Which firmware removes local access is still unsourced. scripts/test_philips_air_coap_spec.py.

Schema gaps that came up, each in its spec's remaining_unknowns: no binary socket-frame or Modbus register block (SolarEdge, AirPort), no "register × 10^scale-factor" state mapping for entities, no field for a one-client-at-a-time device, no CoAP transport block or encrypted-CoAP body scheme (Philips), no DHCP discovery method, and no way to tie a command to a variant.

docs.title: 2026-11-06 (research follow-up)
docs.text: A review of the newly consolidated research packs against the merged catalogue. Two uncovered read-only protocols were promoted, and one existing spec gained substantial corrections. Every new or updated spec remains testing: untested; upstream tests and public captures are not relabelled as hardware verification by this project.

docs.text: Spec Origin Notes Quicklynks BM2 Two public BM2 clients, 2026-11-03 Active FFF4 encrypted voltage/percentage/status notifications, enhanced and legacy advertisements, strict validation and staleness rules. History, configuration and BM6 are excluded. scripts/test_quicklynks_bm2_spec.py. WaterRower ComModule / SmartRow FTMS profile + V3.10 capture-backed SmartRow follow-up ComModule stays on standard FTMS. SmartRow gets its actual 0x1234 service, checksummed ASCII telemetry, session commands, keylock transform and 24-point raw force curve. The ComModule f364 extension and calibrated force/work units remain unresolved. scripts/test_waterrower_smartrow_spec.py.

docs.title: Existing-device corrections
docs.text: • Oral-B iO Smart Brush: charger characteristics now live in the recovered a0f03e00 service rather than the brush service. Added the captured native and 0x37 passthrough grammar, charger status bits, length-gated FF05, protocol-7/8 FF29 retained-session record, ServiceDataA/B and V008+ SonosMetadata. Provisioning writes, protocol-6 FF29 and unresolved units stay open. Added the missing user guide and scripts/test_oral_b_io_smartbrush_spec.py.

docs.title: Evaluated but not promoted yet
docs.text:
• Big Ass Fans: both legacy SenseME ASCII/UDP and newer clear-TCP SLIP/protobuf exist in the recovered app, but model/firmware selection needs hardware evidence. Do not send both protocols as a discovery probe.
  • Furbo: ongoing control is authenticated TUTK P2P, not simply cloud-only, and some Furbo 2 units expose authenticated RTSP. An offline path using account-exported credentials is not yet established, nor is a current-model RTSP/ONVIF contract. A full local-control spec would overstate the evidence.
  • Ecowitt gateways: four local HTTP reads are well supported, but several weather/rain/light field and unit mappings conflict between clients. A future spec should preserve raw IDs and units rather than inventing normalization.
  • Eye-Fi: the consolidated receiver, credential and TAR findings improve the existing research trail, but hardware discovery/retry and reset-card provisioning still need validation. No outbound camera-client spec is added.

docs.title: Added this week
docs.text:
Two Do these next picks and one candidate from the 2026-10-25 sweep. Every spec is testing: untested; wire facts from client code are reported.

Spec Source Notes Yogasleep Dohm Connect 2026-10-25 candidate One vendor service (00005600-d102-11e1-9b23-00025b005aa5) with one write+notify characteristic. ASCII commands ending in $: device ID (i$, which every other command needs), power, speed 1–10, name, clock and the three schedule slots, with the reply grammar. Replies carry no request IDs, so a client reads back after writes. t and I are hypothesis, and I (change the ID) is advanced. One power switch entity. Upstream's example device ID is replaced with one derived from a documentation MAC. scripts/test_yogasleep_dohm_connect_spec.py. Hasbro Furby Connect #23 Name-only advertisement, the vendor service dab91435-… with eight characteristics, and the Nordic legacy DFU service. Action addressing at four levels, antenna colour, eye backlight, mood meters, name, the sensor stream start/stop and the keep-quiet write every 3 s. The DLC upload is described as a procedure only; announce, delete and bootloader entry are advanced. No Hasbro content is reproduced. bluefluff and PyFluff agree, but PyFluff is a port of bluefluff, so that confirms transcription, not the wire. scripts/test_hasbro_furby_connect_spec.py. Nissan Leaf Battery Data (ZE0 / AZE0 / ZE1) #24 Strictly read-only. The battery controller on 0x79B→0x7BB plus VCM and meter, the ELM327 setup and flow-control commands the open client uses, ISO-TP reassembly, 21 group polls (01/02/04/06/61/62/83/84) and VCM/meter 22 reads. Group 01 has separate decode tables per generation, identified by reply length. A safety_advisory (caution) carries the sources' polling cautions (relay clicks with the car off; the battery controller drops overlapping requests). Writes such as fault clearing and the state-of-health reset are named by service only and left out. Several ZE0/AZE0 offsets are hypothesis. scripts/test_nissan_leaf_obd2_spec.py.

Schema gaps that came up, each in its spec's remaining_unknowns or protocol_details: a BLE parameter cannot take its value from another command's reply (Dohm's device ID), no ASCII-decimal number encoding for templates (Dohm), no write-only light or number entity (Furby), one characteristic carrying several reply types (Furby), and on the OBD side 1-byte group ids in data_identifiers, per-request ECU addressing, multi-field response layouts and variant identification by reply length (Leaf).
